paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 20/11/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, in the 20:47 UTC reading, Polymarket pays 45.65 and Kalshi 51.00. In the polls with fieldwork up to 17/11, she is first in all 86 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, with 27% to 40%, and she leads in the 39 runoff matchups in which she was tested, with 52% to 70%. The two most recent polls in the database are still YouGov's for Le HuffPost, with fieldwork from 12 to 17/11, and Ifop-Fiducial's for TF1-LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11. On 20/11, the Commission des sondages published notice 10392, from Ifop-Fiducial for Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 2 to 4/11; the database has not structured it yet, and it is not in this screen's counts. Le Pen's appeal against ineligibility at the Cour de cassation is due to be decided by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 18.1 across 47 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days and is among the top two in 80 of the 86 lists of the last 45 days; in the 14 runoff matchups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, with 30% to 39%. In the win contract, he is at 14.50 on Polymarket and 13.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names in the top five of both markets appear in fewer than half of the lists in the poll database: David Lisnard in 40 of the 86 of the last 45 days, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 17.75, and at 17.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he is not among the top two in any of the 40 lists and averages 9.1 across 31 lists from 7 pollsters over the last 30 days. Lagarde is 4th on Polymarket, at 5.55, and at 5.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are from Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 9 and 10/11, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 29/10, the European Central Bank announced that she leaves the bank's presidency on 07/02/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 09/11, is at 1.35 on Polymarket and 1.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 5 of the 86 lists, one from each of 5 pollsters, with 2% to 4.5%; in the two most recent, he has 3% in YouGov's and 4% in Ifop's.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than three times Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 12.5 over the last 30 days, across 33 lists from 7 pollsters, and Glucksmann 11.7, across 46 lists from 7 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe is among the top two in 3 of 60, and Glucksmann in 3 of 81. In the win contract, Philippe is at 5.50 on Polymarket and 4.60 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.45 and 1.00.

**In the 18:25 UTC press collection of 20/11, five of the ten headlines, from 7 outlets, are about Dominique de Villepin's candidacy, announced that day.** At a press conference at the Maison de l'Amérique latine, in Paris, the former prime minister said "Je suis candidat"; Libération and BFMTV report the announcement, L'Opinion notes a programme of 258 measures and posters with the slogan "Et si on s'aimait encore", Les Echos writes that he wants to embody an alternative to Macronism and to the duel between the RN and LFI, and Le Figaro reviews his polling. To be on the ballot, he must gather 500 sponsorships from elected officials by 12/03/2027. Villepin appears in 14 of the 86 lists of the last 45 days, with 1% to 3%, and in the win contract he is at 3.15 on Polymarket and 1.30 on Kalshi; in the reading of 19/11 at 23:10 UTC, Polymarket paid 2.15. Le Monde covers a study by Cevipof for the Association of Mayors of France, published on 20/11, in which almost half of the mayors surveyed say they would refuse a request for sponsorship. BFMTV shows Jad Zahab, Gabriel Attal's spokesman, saying the aim is not to create a single party but to avoid 5 or 6 candidacies in the central space. In an interview with Ouest-France, Jean Massiet, host of the political programme Backseat, calls the Arcom rule announced on 19/11, which requires content creators to respect pluralism during the campaign, an "écran de fumée" (smokescreen). Ouest-France also interviews Jérôme Baloge, mayor of Niort, who is part of Édouard Philippe's campaign team, and Le Monde publishes an analysis of the fight over the "tactical vote".

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
